prompt:
TEASER | SHOT T01 | THE EMPTY HOUSE
DURATION: 15 SECONDS
FORMAT: HORIZONTAL 16:9
SHOT STRUCTURE: ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE


LOCATION REFERENCE

The sisters’ private room: {{LOC_PRIVATE_ROOM}}

Preserve the referenced architecture, doorway, furnishings,
plants, curtains, materials and warm domestic character.

The room is empty of people.
Its ordinary warmth remains intact.


PROP REFERENCE

The musician’s broken instrument: {{PROP_INSTRUMENT_BROKEN}}

Preserve the exact instrument design and its established broken state.

One broken instrument lies on the floor inside the room.
Its body and detached pieces belong to the same single object.
They remain in fixed positions throughout the shot.

One loosened string remains attached at one end.


VISIBLE ELEMENTS AND STARTING STATE

The half-open entrance door occupies the RIGHT foreground.
The open gap lies between the door’s free edge and the LEFT jamb.

Through this gap, reveal:
a section of the warm room,
one empty chair in the LEFT middle distance,
plants deeper inside,
and part of a softly moving curtain.

The broken instrument lies approximately 1.5 meters beyond
the threshold, just to the RIGHT of the initial sightline.

At the beginning, the door leaf physically conceals the instrument.

The door remains at the same half-open angle throughout.
Camera movement gradually reveals what lies behind its edge.

Every visible chair and doorway remains unoccupied.
The cat exists only as an off-screen sound.


LIGHTING

Soft warm daylight enters through the room’s established window.
Preserve the location reference’s natural light direction.

The corridor side of the doorway is dimmer than the room.
The door edge creates a dark foreground boundary around
the warm interior.

Natural light reveals fabric, leaves, the floor and the broken
instrument with restrained contrast.

Maintain consistent illumination and exposure.
The atmosphere remains domestic and physically ordinary.


CAMERA

One continuous 35mm shot.
Camera height approximately 45 centimeters above the floor.

Begin outside the room, looking through the half-open doorway.
Use restrained handheld balance with almost imperceptible
organic instability.

The camera moves slowly forward and slightly LEFT,
through the existing open gap.

This movement creates physical parallax around the stationary
door edge and reveals the instrument on the right.

Keep useful depth of field:
the room is readable initially;
the broken instrument becomes the clearest subject as it appears.


00:00–00:05 — THE UNDISTURBED ROOM

Hold the low view through the doorway with a very slow
forward creep.

The empty chair remains in the left middle distance.
Plants and warm domestic textures occupy the deeper room.

A curtain moves slightly in a faint indoor draft.
Everything else remains settled.

The instrument is still concealed by the right foreground door leaf.

Sound consists of quiet interior room tone and faint curtain movement.


00:05–00:11 — THE DISCOVERY

Continue the same slow movement:
approximately 50 centimeters forward and 20 centimeters left,
remaining within the clear doorway gap.

As the lens passes the door’s free edge,
the broken instrument gradually becomes visible on the floor
in the LOWER-RIGHT and CENTRAL part of the composition.

The reveal happens entirely through camera parallax.

Allow a small downward reframing so the broken body,
its separated pieces and the attached loose string are readable.

The warm room remains visible beyond the object.

The instrument stays motionless.
A faint draft causes the free end of the loosened string
to brush softly against the instrument’s body,
producing one fragile metallic tick.

The camera slows as the damage becomes clear.


00:11–00:15 — THE UNSEEN SOUND

Stop the forward movement.
Hold on the broken instrument within the quiet room.

At approximately 12 seconds, one short, distant cat meow
comes from somewhere OFF-SCREEN LEFT, deeper inside the house.

Keep the sound acoustically distant and slightly muffled.
Its exact location remains unresolved.

After a brief reaction delay, the camera begins a small,
hesitant pan LEFT toward the sound.

The instrument drifts toward the right edge of the composition.
Only more empty interior space begins to enter from the left.

Interrupt this searching movement before its destination is revealed.

At exactly 15 seconds, cut directly to solid black.
Cut the room tone to silence at the same instant.


VISUAL AND SOUND RESTRAINT

The frame contains architecture, furnishings, plants
and the single broken instrument.

Reflections and visible shadows belong only to these objects.

The tension comes from the gradual discovery of damage
inside an otherwise warm, ordinary room.

Use real-time motion, tactile surfaces and restrained exposure.

Sound:
quiet room tone,
faint curtain movement,
one delicate string contact,
one distant off-screen cat meow,
then silence.

NO MUSIC. NO DIALOGUE.

Established requirements for this subject:
- No human appears without a mask. Every person on screen, including nobles, gift-bearers, servants and background figures, wears a mask. A figure who is not a named character takes one of the masked caste looks in REF-001, Civilization Caste Board. Never show a bare human face.

<<<image_1>>> is Jamshid Daughters Chamber (LOC-020 V01); match it wherever Jamshid Daughters Chamber appears.
<<<image_2>>> is Instrument Saz (PRP-018 V01); match it wherever Instrument Saz appears.
